top_story: By 1 June, the sharpest regional shift is on Israel’s northern front, where Israeli forces have pushed deeper into Lebanese territory and the threat of strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs has revived Lebanese fears of a renewed occupation. That military pressure lands in a region already primed for wider escalation after Tehran’s March vow to expand confrontation if Washington targeted Iran’s power infrastructure over Hormuz, raising the risk that any Lebanon flare-up could fold into a broader Iran-linked conflict. Beneath these interstate pressures, the killing of 15-year-old Kawthar al-Husayjawi in Iraq for refusing marriage to her cousin exposes a parallel crisis of coercion and impunity that continues to shape daily life far from formal front lines. The regional picture is not only one of military escalation but of deepening insecurity for civilians, as war threats and entrenched social violence reinforce each other across the Middle East.
